source_evidence.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Compare squared increments of two Itô rows. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source_evidence.statement: For each of finitely many coordinates, integrate two progressive square-integrable integrands against the same coordinate Brownian motion. Sum the resulting coordinate integrals to form each row. The difference of their squared-increment sums is integrable, and its expected absolute value is bounded uniformly over finite deterministic grids.
source_evidence.formula: \begin{gathered}R_f(t)=\sum_{j\in J} I_j(f_j)(t),\qquad Q(f)=\sum_i(\Delta_i R_f)^2,\\ E(f)=\sum_{j\in J}\|f_j\|_{L^2(\Omega\times[0,T],\,\mu\otimes dt)}^2,\\ \int |Q(\eta)-Q(\xi)|\,d\mu\le |J|\sqrt{E(\eta+\xi)}\,\sqrt{E(\eta-\xi)}.\end{gathered}
assumptions: On a positive finite time horizon, the given filtration and finite sample measure satisfy the usual conditions used to construct the completed Itô integral.
The grid lies in [0,T] and is nondecreasing. The coordinate index type J is finite and may be empty.
For each j, both integrands are real, progressive and square integrable. They share the same Brownian motion Bⱼ relative to the given filtration. The drivers at different indices may be dependent.
source_evidence.boundary: The inequality compares the two actual row processes on any common deterministic grid. The squared-increment limit needs a separate proof for an approximating family.

steps.title: Factor the difference of squares
steps.text: At the two deterministic endpoints in each cell, linearity identifies the increments of the sum and difference of the integrands. Multiply these two increments and add over cells.
steps.formula: Q(\eta)-Q(\xi)=\sum_i U_iV_i\quad\mu\text{-a.e.},\qquad U_i=\Delta_i R_{\eta+\xi},\quad V_i=\Delta_i R_{\eta-\xi}.
steps.assessment: The stated mathematical move and formula agree with the current proof and its hypotheses.

steps.title: Apply Cauchy–Schwarz twice
steps.text: Each row increment is in L² by the scalar cell isometries and finite summation. The products are therefore integrable, as is the signed difference. Bound the absolute value of the finite sum by the sum of the absolute products. Apply integral Cauchy–Schwarz in each cell, then finite Cauchy–Schwarz to the resulting list of square roots.
steps.assessment: The stated mathematical move and formula agree with the current proof and its hypotheses.

steps.title: Control the row energies
steps.text: Cauchy–Schwarz across the coordinates bounds the square of each row increment by the coordinate count times the sum of the coordinate squares. Apply the exact scalar grid isometry to each coordinate and enlarge the grid span to [0,T]. Each square root contributes a factor √|J|.
steps.assessment: The stated mathematical move and formula agree with the current proof and its hypotheses.
